body:
Fiber v2.32.0 and up support adding 404 handling by customizing the error handler. You can take a look https://docs.gofiber.io/extra/faq#how-do-i-handle-custom-404-responses

I'll also think how to fix the problem.

unfortunately you are right and we have to do some rebuilding

the problem is that the routing tree has wrong positions in our routing tree because we don't remember at what time the mount command was executed

because we wanted to allow routes to be added later, we moved the merge to the start of the app, but currently we don't know where the mount command was executed

we already have some ideas and will try to fix this in the next release
I'll try to fix this weekend or next week.

issue.title: Breaking change to mounting caused by PR #2120

repository.name: fiber
repository.description: ⚡️ Express inspired web framework written in Go

issue.body:
### Bug Description

When mounting a separate application, routes are skipped with valid prefixing and return invalid request URL. Appears in versions > 2.40.0, and seems to be caused by #2120

Specifically, the bug is caused when creating an app out of the main initialization of the (main) fiver application, and sub-mounting to a path (non-prefixed and prefixed, eg below)

### How to Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Define a function to create a *fiber.App 
```go
func CreatesApp() *fiber.App {
    app := fiber.New
    app.Get(“sub”, func(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
          log.Print(“called”)
          return c.JSON(“ok”)
}

    return app
}
```

2. Mount in main app: 

```go

func main(){
   mainApp := fiber.New()
   subApp := submodule.CreatesApp()
   mainApp.Mount(“/path”, subApp)
   ….
}
```

3. Try a request to ‘path/sub’, it will fail


### Expected Behavior

Pre 2.40.0, no issues & sub-paths route as expected. Fixes by rolling back to 2.39.0

### Fiber Version

2.40.0

### Code Snippet (optional)

```go
package main

import "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
import "log"

func CreatesApp() *fiber.App {
    app := fiber.New()

    app.Get(‘bar’, func(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
    return c.JSON(‘ok’)
}

    return app
}

func main() {
  app := fiber.New()
  sub := CreatesApp()
  app.Mount(
   “foo”, sub
  )
  log.Print(sub.MountPath()) // prints “foo”
  log.Fatal(app.Listen(":3000"))
}
```
